scope: 1996 classic English base game, publisher rules pp. 1–12

independence.not_reviewed: No other reviews, grades, or history were read.
independence.authority: Publisher-rule transcription; the answer key and summary are comparison artifacts, not independent authority.

grading_principles: Grade the question actually asked. A fact appearing in the expected answer is not automatically a required answer component.
Evaluate each answer on its own; no missing restriction is supplied from another answer.
An omitted incidental restriction differs from an affirmative overbroad permission.

The rulebook generally distinguishes board regions from the Castillo; wording that identifies non-King origin regions need not repeat a separate Castillo parenthetical unless the question requests that distinction or the answer affirmatively allows Castillo removal.
When English source wording leaves a quantifier unresolved, identify that ambiguity rather than claiming an unstated legal example is expressly authorized.

source_findings.finding: The board has nine regions and a separate Castillo space. The secret disk omits the Castillo.

source_findings.section: The following applies to all cards, A and C
source_findings.finding: The King’s region cannot receive or supply pieces, but may be scored. Caballeros may enter the Castillo during movement; removal from Castillo occurs only at general scoring.

source_findings.section: Intrigue: up to five from any one region
source_findings.finding: Up to five own and/or foreign pieces move from one non-King region to other non-King regions and/or the Castillo.

source_findings.section: Intrigue: any three foreign; any three; any four own; any four
source_findings.finding: Three-foreign permits up to three foreign pieces from any non-King regions to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. Any-three permits own and/or foreign pieces with the same any-regions wording. The four-piece descriptions say any other regions for destinations. Multiple source regions are permitted; no example explains whether other excludes every source region collectively or only each moving piece’s own source.

source_findings.section: Pick one region; choose any region; each secretly chooses a region
source_findings.finding: The individual pick-one action expressly permits King’s region and Castillo. The collective secret action uses disks and scores only uniquely selected regions. Special Castillo scoring leaves its pieces there; that consequence does not change which locations can be selected.

adjudications.rationale: The answer directly covers every requested comparison: different owners are allowed, the pieces all come from one origin, and destinations are other non-King regions and/or Castillo. The question asks whether origins may be multiple; it does not separately ask to enumerate forbidden source locations. Not repeating the King/Castillo source exclusions is therefore not a missing requested ruling.

Mixed ownership, one origin, and other non-King regions/Castillo destinations are all correct. With only one source region, cannot return to the origin accurately states the other-regions restriction. Do not add a missing-source-exclusion penalty for facts not separately requested here.

All requested rulings are correct. The answer additionally and accurately identifies both protected source locations. These extra details are supported, but their presence does not make them mandatory solely because they appear in the key.

All four expressly requested rulings are correct. The limited downgrade concerns the answer’s additional affirmative source claim: they may come from any regions, with no King-region qualification anywhere in this answer. Taken as a statement of source legality, this grants more than the publisher’s any regions except the King’s. This is not a penalty for failing to repeat an incidental expected-answer fact. If grading is restricted strictly to the four asked yes/no/destination rulings and disregards ancillary source assertions, those rulings alone merit correct.
adjudications.Castillo_ruling: Do not treat the absence of a separate not-Castillo clause as a second error. In this answer regions are distinguished from Castillo destinations; it does not expressly authorize removing Castillo pieces.
adjudications.grade_sensitivity: The only downgrade depends on reading from any regions as affirmative unrestricted source permission rather than shorthand for the requested multi-origin flexibility. The source prohibition itself is unambiguous; the answer’s intended scope is the uncertainty.

adjudications.rationale: The answer supplies both maxima, own/foreign ownership, flexible non-King board-region origins, and the distinct any-regions/other-regions destination wording. It does not affirm Castillo as a source. Given the source’s board-region/Castillo distinction, non-King origin regions adequately describes the origin domain; a separate not-Castillo parenthetical is clarification rather than a required additional ruling. This interpretation uses this answer’s wording and the source, not another reader answer.

Both maxima, ownership flexibility, non-King region origins, and the source’s different three/four destination formulations are present. Other-regions wording is preserved without the additional each-origin quantifier appearing in Q51. The answer contrasts regions with Castillo destinations and does not authorize Castillo removal; a missing explicit Castillo-source parenthetical alone does not warrant partial credit.

The core answer is correct. The final each-origin phrase, read literally, universally excludes all source regions as destinations for every moved piece. With pieces from A and B it forbids an A-to-B move as well as a B-to-A move. A per-piece reading of other regions only forbids a piece staying in its own source and would permit those cross-source moves. Those propositions are not equivalent. The publisher text says from any regions into any other regions but supplies neither an explicit all-source exclusion nor a multi-origin example resolving the quantifier. Partial reflects an unqualified stronger assertion on a requested restriction, not a source-proven finding that cross-source movement is definitely legal.
adjudications.exact_ambiguity: Does other regions mean destinations outside the union of all origins used in the action, or a destination different from the respective origin of each moved Caballero? The authorized pp. 1–12 source does not explicitly resolve that distinction.
adjudications.recommended_wording: Move up to four own Caballeros from any non-King board regions, never from Castillo, into other non-King regions and/or Castillo. Preserve the publisher’s other-regions wording; do not assert an all-origins ban without further authority.
adjudications.grading_limit: Do not label the whole answer incorrect, and do not count the four-own allowance or protected source/destination rules as wrong. If the answer is interpreted as informal per-piece shorthand, correct is defensible; its literal universal quantifier is why this report selects partial.

adjudications.rationale: The question asks a selection-domain comparison between two scoring cards. The answer correctly gives nine disk regions including the King’s region, excludes Castillo for that disk action, and permits both King’s region and Castillo for the individual pick-one card. Whether Castillo pieces are subsequently redistributed is a separate scoring consequence, not part of the requested selection-domain comparison. Its absence is not a basis for partial credit. Applying normal scoring rules does not affirm redistribution.
adjudications.incidental_key_fact: No Castillo redistribution is true but unrequested here. Q16 and Q34 separately ask that issue; their existence does not expand Q52 or permit borrowing answers.

summary.decisive_caveat: Q51’s cross-source quantifier is not explicitly resolved by the permitted source; Q48 readerB is grade-sensitive to whether its extra any-regions assertion is read literally or confined to the question’s multi-origin comparison.
